$comment: QUARANTINE LIST for `npm run test:gate`.
Every entry names one test that is suppressed, WHAT FAILURE it suppresses,
WHY, and WHEN the suppression expires. The runner (tools/test-gate.mjs)
prints this table on every run and fails once an entry is past `expires` —
a quarantine that cannot expire is just deletion with extra steps.
── `matches` is required, and it is the point of this file ──
Until 2026-09-10 an entry described its failure in PROSE and nothing checked
the prose against reality. Suppression worked by NAME: the test was skipped
outright, so it produced no output that could disagree with the description.
A quarantined test that began failing for an entirely different reason
inherited the existing entry in silence. Two entries on this list had stated
reasons that were simply false, and one was read by an auditor and relayed to
the owner as a live security hole. Prose cannot go stale loudly.
`matches` is a distinctive fragment of the ACTUAL failure output — a literal
substring, or `/regex/` if the output carries volatile content. The gate no
longer skips anything; it runs every test and then adjudicates:
fails + output contains `matches`  → suppressed.
fails + output does NOT match      → RED. A DIFFERENT failure is hiding
here. Both signatures are printed.
passes (and class is not `flaky`)  → RED. Delete the entry.
never ran / renamed / source-skip  → RED. The entry names nothing.
no `matches` at all                → RED, before any test runs.
Derive `matches` from output you have actually SEEN, never from your
description of it. When the gate reports an unsuppressed failure it prints
the real signature — copy that. Absolute paths, timings and long hashes are
normalised away before matching, so a signature does not rot when the
checkout moves or a test gets slower.
`class` is the honest label for what the suppression is hiding:
stale-fixture  — the test pins behaviour a later, deliberate change replaced.
The code is right; the assertion is out of date.
runner-mismatch— the test is in the wrong runner (JSX under the non-JSX
config). It passes under `npm run test:ui`.
OPEN-GAP       — the test is RIGHT and the code is WRONG. Suppressed only so
the gate can land green today. These are real defects; read
them first.
flaky          — genuinely non-deterministic. The ONLY class exempt from the
passes-check, because it passes sometimes by definition. It
is NOT exempt from carrying `matches`.
Established from the 2026-08-11 baseline: 5,927 tests, 5,867 pass, 39 fail,
21 skipped. One of those 39 (the storage-disclosure invariant) was FIXED in
the same PR rather than quarantined.
Swept entry-by-entry against main (152bbbac) on 2026-09-10: 37 entries
examined, 36 still failing with the signatures recorded below, 1 deleted for
passing (the /style page V0/v0 banned-string check, which now passes across
all 2,821 generated cases).
── `expires` is PER ENTRY, and the top-level one is now only a CAP ──
Until 2026-09-11 all 35 suppressions sat behind the single top-level
`expires` below. One shared date means the whole list falls off a cliff on
one day, and a cliff gets bulk-extended rather than reviewed — the exact
outcome an expiry date exists to prevent. `tools/test-gate.mjs` even names
the blanket re-date as the failure mode, and then made it the only
affordance the file had.
Every entry now carries its own `expires`. THE RULE USED, so the next
reader can re-derive it rather than trust it:
1. Creation date cannot stagger anything, and that is itself a finding.
All 35 entries were added in ONE commit (c84deafd, 2026-08-11), the
baseline sweep. `git log -S<test name> -- tests/quarantine.json`
returns 2026-08-11 for all 35. A shared expiry was structurally
inevitable given how the list was born.
2. So the stagger is keyed to the REMEDIATION UNIT — the test file,
because a file is the smallest thing one PR closes. 35 entries
collapse to 19 units. The single OPEN-GAP is broken out of its file
(registry-truth.test.ts) because closing it is a manifest row plus a
product decision, not an assertion rewrite.
3. Units are ordered by how well-understood the root cause is. The seven
auto-registry units go first: route.ts deliberately stopped naming
functions, the correct assertion already exists elsewhere, and the fix
is the same edit seven times. The OPEN-GAP goes last.
4. Slots run 2026-09-20 → 2026-11-09. NOTHING moves later than the
2026-11-09 the whole list already had; the last slot IS that date.
Restructuring may not weaken a suppression, so the cap is enforced in
the runner: an entry whose `expires` is past the top-level value fails
validation before a single test runs.
The spacing that falls out is ~2.8 days between units. That is not a
design choice, it is the arithmetic of 19 remediation units against 50 days
of remaining runway, and it is the honest reading of this file: the list is
too long for the window it has left.

entries.test: property-management-rent-collection-chase (runtime:live) is sweep-dispatched OR non-sweep caller-covered
entries.matches: appears in NEITHER SWEEP_DISPATCH_MANIFEST nor NON_SWEEP_LIVE_SKILLS
entries.reason: REAL, but the previous reason was FALSE and is retracted. It said 'it claims to fire and nothing fires it'. The sweep IS registered and DOES fire: lib/inngest/functions/property-management-rent-collection-chase-sweep.ts exists, and lib/inngest/registry.ts auto-derives the function list from the filesystem via require.context — a file under lib/inngest/functions/ is registered BY EXISTING. Its cron is RENT_COLLECTION_CHASE_SWEEP_CRON = '0 12 * * *'; the sweep then no-ops unless BUILDIUM_ADAPTER_LIVE=on (step 0 of its own header). The real gap is that the skill is absent from the hand-maintained SWEEP_DISPATCH_MANIFEST / NON_SWEEP_LIVE_SKILLS rows this test reads — a missing-manifest-row COPY gap, not a caller gap. Still a genuine failure (the manifest does not describe the fleet), so it stays quarantined. NOTE, closed 2026-09-11: lib/claims/known-drift.ts:71 used to assert the opposite ('the one entry here that is a caller gap rather than a copy gap'). It has been corrected, and so has the home-services entry beside it, which made the same 'no caller' claim about a skill that lib/inngest/functions/home-services-estimate-followup-sweep.ts fires daily at 09:00 UTC. Both are now pinned by lib/claims/known-drift-reasons.test.ts, which fails if any reason asserts nothing fires a skill that a registered sweep file names — so this cross-file note can no longer rot without a red.
